ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.Our aim is to make student contributions: ClassMic would let an instructor approve a student’s phone as a classroom microphone. We will build a small browser prototype and test whether it makes questions easier to hear without slowing the discussion.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.A question from one student can help the: A question from one student can help the whole class only if others hear it. When a voice does not carry across the room, the instructor may need to repeat the question or wait while a microphone reaches the student. We have not yet measured how often this happens in our classes.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.ClassMic addresses the CONNECT theme thr: The project supports the CONNECT theme by helping students hear and respond to one another during class.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.The proposed concept uses an instructor-: The prototype will use existing Wi-Fi and speakers, with only one phone transmitting at a time. We will test audio delay and ask volunteer reviewers whether it improves audibility.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.A commercial example, Biamp Crowd Mics,: Biamp Crowd Mics already offers phone microphones and moderator controls [1]. It provides a commercial alternative to consider alongside the prototype and current classroom practice.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.For students and instructors who find pe: Students would join a temporary session, request a turn and speak through the room speakers after instructor approval. The instructor could mute the microphone or end the session. The intended benefit is clearer questions with less time spent passing a microphone.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.The course project covers requirements,: The course project covers requirements, a small prototype, controlled tests and a recommendation. Development will use two weekly sprints. A classroom rollout, paid infrastructure or a longer institutional pilot would require a separate decision.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.Temiko leads the prototype. Nurtore coor: Proposed roles: Temiko leads development and testing. Nurtore coordinates requirements and delivery.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.Review the revised idea, charter and cou: Review the project scope and assess course deliverables.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.Review device, network, sound and access: Advise on device compatibility, room sound and accessibility if a room test can be arranged.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.Proposed evaluation targets include a 95: The one-way audio-delay target is a 95th percentile of 150 milliseconds or less. The remaining targets are listed below.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.Complete five priority user stories and: Complete five priority user stories and pass all required acceptance checks.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.At least 75% positive feedback from at l: At least 75% positive feedback from at least 5 volunteer reviewers. Include the response counts.
ClassMic_A2_Aspiration.ClassMic is a classroom microphone conce: ClassMic lets students request a speaking turn from their phones. After instructor approval, their voice plays through the room speakers. We want to test whether this makes questions easier to hear without slowing the discussion. In two weekly sprints, we will build a small prototype, test it with volunteers and decide whether a larger pilot is worth pursuing.

ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.GO for a limited course prototype using: GO for a two-sprint course prototype using existing equipment. We will test whether students can speak clearly through their phones while the instructor controls the queue. A funded classroom pilot remains at REVISE until we establish local demand, audio performance, support needs and the cost of commercial alternatives.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.The decision sought is authorization to: We request approval to develop and evaluate the prototype with an estimated 100 student hours. We plan no additional cash spending, assuming the team has enough time and the required equipment is available.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Expected value is easier audibility and: The expected benefit is clearer questions with fewer pauses to repeat a question or pass a microphone. Local demand and performance still need testing, so we cannot yet estimate gains in participation or financial savings.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.The phone microphone concept and intende: Phone microphones with instructor approval and stop controls.
Five priority user stories built in two weekly sprints.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Local price, room fit and comparison wit: Local price, classroom fit and performance compared with the prototype.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Benefit must be demonstrated against the: Test audibility and ease of use against the current speaking process.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.No new platform. Staff time and equipmen: Uses existing teaching practices and equipment. Staff time still matters.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Proposed 100 student hours. No increment: Estimated 100 student hours and AED 0 additional cash. Long-term maintenance is outside the estimate.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Control data capture and avoid saved spe: Require microphone permission and instructor control. Store no audio.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.No-install browser access is a hypothesi: Test whether students can join and use the browser workflow easily.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.A custom prototype fits the course requi: Building a prototype meets the course requirement to develop and evaluate selected user stories. A later campus decision should also compare a commercial product with improvements to current classroom practice.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Reviewed project direction, requirements: Project scope, requirements and schedule reviewed before development.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Temporary sessions, permission flow, que: Session access, microphone permissions, speaking queue and instructor controls.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Integrate audio, test misuse and recover: Audio integration, misuse and recovery tests, volunteer feedback and the product report.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Assess delivery against the charter and: Assess results against the project objectives and prepare the final recommendation.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Planning review is scheduled for 18 Sept: The proposed plan review is on 18 September, followed by two weekly sprints. The planning assignment is due 22 September at 00:00. Development, testing and the product report must finish by 2 October for the report deadline of 3 October at 00:00. Execution evidence is due 4 October at 00:00 and closing work on 10 October at 00:00.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.The cash forecast is AED 0, conditional: The AED 0 cash estimate assumes we can reuse available phones, a laptop, speakers and permitted tools. The 100 student hours are an effort estimate; no hourly pay rate has been assigned. Paid hosting, equipment or account upgrades would require a revised budget and approval.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.The selected prototype target is a 95th: We will measure one-way audio delay in 30 trials, aiming for a 95th percentile of 150 ms or less. Tests must also check whether speech is intelligible and whether speaker feedback occurs.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.All Must checks. 9/10 setups within 2 mi: All required checks must pass, with no open critical defect. At least 9/10 setups within 2 minutes, 27/30 speaking trials within 3 seconds and 75% positive feedback from at least 5 reviewers.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.Feedback or network delay may make the a: Speaker feedback or long network delays could make speech hard to follow. Some phones or browsers may be incompatible, and weak instructor controls could allow unwanted transmission. Limited team time or unavailable reviewers could reduce testing. Stop tests if control or privacy fails, keep a physical microphone or instructor repetition as a fallback, and reduce optional work if time is short.
ClassMic_B2_Business_Case.The present evidence supports a bounded: Proceed with the course prototype using available equipment and an estimated 100 student hours. Consider a larger pilot only if the tests show clearer questions, reliable instructor control and a feasible support plan.

ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Proposed project charter. ClassMic will: Proposed charter for a ClassMic browser prototype, developed and evaluated in two weekly sprints.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Test whether student phones can make cla: The project will test whether student phones can make classroom questions easier to hear while the instructor controls speaking turns. We will compare the prototype with the current speaking process before recommending a larger pilot. This supports the CONNECT theme through classroom discussion.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Complete five priority user stories. Pas: Complete five priority user stories. Pass all required acceptance checks with no open critical defect.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.At least 75% positive audibility feedbac: At least 75% positive audibility feedback from at least 5 volunteer reviewers. Include response counts and sample limitations.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Zero unauthorized transmissions in misus: Zero unauthorized transmissions in misuse tests. No saved audio or transcripts. Keep a physical microphone or instructor repetition available.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Use scripted trials with a ready speaker: Use scripted trials with a ready speaker to measure setup and speaking activation. Measure one-way audio delay separately and report its median and 95th percentile. The 95th-percentile target is 150 milliseconds or less; the three-second activation target includes the time from instructor approval until speech is audible.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Excluded: live teaching deployment, a si: Excluded: live teaching deployment, an extended classroom pilot, recording or transcripts, permanent profiles, speech-based grading or attendance, simultaneous microphones, remote learning and paid production infrastructure.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Reviewed project direction, requirements: Project purpose, requirements, scope and development plan reviewed.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Sprint 2 audio prototype, test record, f: Sprint 2 audio prototype, test results, volunteer feedback and product report.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Course cutoffs are 22 September for plan: Course deadlines are 22 September for planning, 3 October for the product report, 4 October for execution evidence and 10 October for closing, all at 00:00. The product report must be ready by the evening of 2 October.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.The browser requests explicit permission: The browser must request microphone permission before capture. Only an instructor-approved participant may transmit. Releasing push to talk, muting, disconnecting or ending the session must stop transmission. Expired sessions must reject access. The prototype will store no audio or transcripts. Delete participant-level test records 30 days after course feedback and retain aggregate results. Students who cannot use the phone workflow must be able to use a physical microphone or ask the instructor to repeat their question.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Risks: feedback, network delay, device i: Risks: speaker feedback, network delay, incompatible devices, unwanted transmission and insufficient testing time. Test the audio path early and keep instructor stop controls. Reduce optional work if the schedule slips. Stop affected tests when a control or privacy failure occurs.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Assumptions: suitable phones, a laptop a: Assumptions: suitable phones, a laptop and a speaker are available; volunteers can review the prototype; the team can provide 100 hours in total; and the course instructor accepts the proposed sequence.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Constraints: two weekly construction spr: Constraints: two weekly development sprints, five priority stories and the course deadlines. The AED 0 cash estimate assumes reuse of existing equipment. New spending and live classroom use require separate approval.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Course acceptance authority: the BUS 201: The BUS 2010 instructor reviews the charter and accepts course deliverables. The charter takes effect after course approval. Main stakeholders are student speakers and listeners, instructors and the project team. IT, AV, privacy and accessibility advisers may support a review if available.
ClassMic_C1_Project_Charter.Planning roles: Nurtore Arynuruly is pro: Proposed roles: Nurtore Arynuruly manages the project and requirements. Temiko Machavariani leads development and technical testing. The project manager tracks work, risks and changes against the agreed requirements. The course instructor reviews material scope and schedule changes. Neither team member may commit university funds or authorize live deployment.
